q: Who wrote 'Gitanjali'?
e: Tagore's Gitanjali won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

q: 'The Discovery of India' was written by:
e: Nehru wrote it while in Ahmednagar Fort prison during 1942-46.

q: National Sports Day in India is observed on:
e: It marks the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand.

q: World Environment Day is observed on:
e: World Environment Day, led by UNEP, is celebrated on 5 June.

q: How many players does a volleyball team have on the court at a time?
e: Each volleyball team plays with 6 players on court.

q: 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of:
o: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
e: Wings of Fire (1999) tells the life story of former President A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

q: Which is the highest civilian award of India?
e: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour.

q: Which is India's highest wartime gallantry award?
e: Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award; Ashoka Chakra is the peacetime equivalent.

q: Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on:
e: It marks the birthday of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

q: International Day of Yoga is observed every year on:
e: The UN declared 21 June, the longest day in the Northern Hemisphere, as Yoga Day.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
e: The UN headquarters is in New York, USA.

q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
e: Indira Gandhi became Prime Minister in 1966.

q: What is the national aquatic animal of India?
e: The Ganges river dolphin was declared the national aquatic animal in 2009.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
e: Weightlifter Karnam Malleswari won bronze at the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

q: The Hindi novel 'Godan' was written by:
e: Godan (1936), a story of a poor farmer, is Premchand's best-known novel.

q: 'Malgudi Days' was written by:
e: R. K. Narayan set many stories in the fictional town of Malgudi.

q: 'A Suitable Boy' is a novel by:
e: Vikram Seth's A Suitable Boy (1993) is one of the longest English novels.

q: The Durand Cup is associated with which sport?
e: The Durand Cup, started in 1888, is one of the oldest football tournaments.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
e: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
e: The IMF and the World Bank are headquartered in Washington D.C.

q: Where is the headquarters of UNESCO?
e: UNESCO is headquartered in Paris, France.

q: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
e: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913; C. V. Raman won in Physics in 1930.

q: The national calendar of India is based on which era?
e: India adopted the Saka calendar as the national calendar on 22 March 1957.

q: The Dronacharya Award is given to:
e: The Dronacharya Award honours coaches who train medal-winning athletes.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to climb Mount Everest?
e: Bachendri Pal reached the summit of Everest on 23 May 1984.

q: National Science Day in India is celebrated on:
e: It marks C. V. Raman's announcement of the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928.

q: Which animal was declared the National Heritage Animal of India in 2010?
e: The Indian elephant was declared the National Heritage Animal in 2010; the tiger is the national animal.

q: The national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is taken from which text?
e: 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.

q: The Hindi epic poem 'Kamayani' was written by:
e: Kamayani (1936) is a major work of the Chhayavad poet Jaishankar Prasad.

q: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL?
e: INTERPOL's General Secretariat is in Lyon, France.
